title: Simple Demonstration of Excess Heat by Pulsed Plasma Electrolysis on Nickel
content: Formation of excess heat by plasma electrolysis has been confirmed in very simple experiments. Plasma electrolysis is performed in an insulated vessel with a nickel cathode and a much larger platinized titanium net anode. The power supply is a standard 230-volt socket coupled to a bridge rectifier giving a pulsed voltage varying between 0 and 230 volts. The electrolyte is 0.5 millimolar K2CO3 in commercial demineralized water. Heat output is measured by determining the amount of water evaporated from the vessel by weighing. The excess heat varied around 50%. The results are not understood, but they are consistent with an Efimov-effect like triple deuterium fusion process: D + D + D => DDD => T + 3He, and D + D + D => DDD => 4He + D + heat. A putative triple D Efimov state with a D-D separation of 0.023 angstrom and an energy around 120-630 eV may have been observed by Badiei, Holmlid et al.
